newsitem.title: USA: MEMC sees Q3 sales down from Q2 level.
newsitem.headline: MEMC sees Q3 sales down from Q2 level.

text.p: MEMC Electronic Materials Inc said Tuesday it expects third quarter results to be hurt by several factors, including a reduction of sales from the $324.3 million level seen in the second quarter.
The company said in a news release it expects sales to be more in line with the $289.8 million reported in the first quarter. The company had $251.2 million in the third quarter 1995.
The company also said it has begun eliminating temporary employees and overtime in manufacturing facilities.

Gross margins for the quarter are expected to be below the 25 percent of sales reported in the third quarter of 1995, due to a lower rate of capacity utilization and start-up costs, the company said, adding that the dollar amount of gross margins should be about the $62.7 million reported a year ago.

Net earnings in the 1996 third quarter will also reflect a significant decrease in the level of contribution from equity in income of joint ventures in comparison to the 1995 third quarter, the company said. This is due to lower sales at PHC, the Korean joint venture, and start-up costs at Taisil, the Taiwanese joint venture, the company said.
"The inventory correction that is taking place in the worldwide semiconductor industry has begun to impact silicon wafer manufacturers," said chief executive Ludger Viefhues.
Robert Sandfort, the wafer-maker's president, said it was difficult to say how long the adverse conditions would continue.
"At this point in time, anticipated sales for the 1996 fourth quarter are significantly below our earlier expectations," he said.

"We continue to be optimistic for the longer term prospects of the industry," Sandfort said. "However, in response to the current rapidly changing environment, we are taking actions to improve efficiencies and reduce costs throughout the company," he added, referring to the job and overtime cuts.
